response.passage: The Olympic Games are a global celebration of sportsmanship, but many people have questions about their history and rules. A common query is whether the modern Olympics have been held continuously since ancient times; in reality, the modern Games were revived in 1896, and they have been interrupted by world wars. Regarding symbols, the five interlocking rings represent the union of the five inhabited continents, not individual founding countries. India’s journey in the Olympics is also a proud one. While many celebrate PV Sindhu’s incredible achievements, it is important to note that Karnam Malleswari was the first Indian woman to win an Olympic medal, securing bronze in weightlifting at the 2000 Sydney Games. Furthermore, the Olympic spirit emphasizes participation and fair play over simply winning at all costs. Fair play extends far beyond just avoiding banned substances; it includes respect for opponents, rules, and the integrity of the sport. Finally, athletes must be extremely cautious with medications. Even if a doctor prescribes a medicine, an athlete is responsible for checking if it contains any banned substances, as ignorance of the ingredients does not excuse a violation of anti-doping rules.
response.summary: This passage clarifies common misconceptions about the history, symbols, and values of the Olympic Games. It highlights key facts about India's Olympic history and the strict responsibilities athletes have regarding anti-doping regulations.
